facts.statement: Mythunga lived during the late Early Cretaceous (Albian age) in Australia.
facts.quote: Mythunga is a potentially dubious genus of anhanguerid pterosaur known from the late Early Cretaceous (Albian age) Toolebuc Formation of Australia.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Mythunga was found in April 1991 by Philip Gilmore in Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: Mythunga is known from a partial skull, holotype QM F18896, found in April 1991 by Philip Gilmore in marine rocks of the late Albian-age Toolebuc Formation at Dunluce Station west of Hughenden, Queensland.

facts.statement: The species Mythunga camara was named and described by Ralph Molnar and R. A. Thulborn in 2007/2008.
facts.quote: The type species Mythunga camara was named and described by Ralph Molnar and R. A. Thulborn in 2007/2008.

facts.statement: The genus name Mythunga refers to the constellation Orion in the local Aboriginal language.
facts.quote: The generic name is that of the constellation Orion in the local Aboriginal language.

facts.statement: Mythunga was redescribed by Adele Pentland and Stephen Poropat in 2018 after further preparation of the specimen.
facts.quote: Mythunga was redescribed by Adele Pentland and Stephen Poropat in 2018, benefiting from further preparation of the specimen.

facts.statement: The fossil parts were three-dimensionally preserved together in a chalk nodule.
facts.quote: They were three-dimensionally preserved, associated in a chalk nodule.

facts.statement: The fossil represents a subadult individual.
facts.quote: It represents a subadult individual.

facts.statement: A 2007 estimate placed the wingspan of Mythunga at 4.7 meters.
facts.quote: The wingspan of Mythunga was estimated in 2007 at 4.7 m.

facts.statement: A 2018 revision suggested a skull length of 80 cm to 1 m and a wingspan of 4 to 6 meters.
facts.quote: In 2018, it was concluded that they had been confused with a maxillary tooth and a replacement tooth and that the skull length was likely between 80 cm and 1 m, with a corresponding wingspan of between 4 and 6 m.

facts.statement: The preserved fossil piece has a length of 263 mm.
facts.quote: The entire piece has a preserved length of 263 mm.

facts.statement: The teeth were relatively short, conical, moderately recurved, and had an oval cross-section.
facts.quote: The teeth are relatively short, conical, and moderately recurved. Their cross-section is oval.

facts.statement: There were at least eight teeth in each maxilla and the dentary.
facts.quote: There are at least eight teeth in each maxilla. That is also the minimum number in the dentary.

facts.statement: The outer sides of the jaws were undulating due to bulging tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The outer sides of the jaws are undulating due to bulging tooth sockets.

facts.statement: Kellner et al. placed Mythunga within the family Anhangueridae in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Kellner et al. placed Mythunga within the Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: A 2019 analysis by Pentland et al. recovered Mythunga as a member of the subfamily Ornithocheirinae, sister to Ferrodraco.
facts.quote: The results of a phylogenetic analysis by Pentland et al. in 2019 recovered Mythunga as a member of the family Ornithocheiridae, more precisely within the subfamily Ornithocheirinae as the sister taxon of Ferrodraco.

facts.statement: Richards et al. erected the clade Mythungini in 2023, which includes Mythunga and other Australian tropeognathines.
facts.quote: In 2023, Richards et al. published a revised diagnosis of the related Thapunngaka, where they also erected the clade Mythungini. The clade comprises all Australian tropeognathines, including Mythunga, the type genus of said clade.

facts.statement: In 2025, Pêgas suggested Mythunga should be considered a nomen dubium because no proposed diagnostic characters were unique to the genus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Pêgas suggested that Mythunga should be classified as a nomen dubium, as the author found none of the proposed diagnostic characters to be unique to this genus, and disagreed with using the tribe Mythungini.

facts.statement: Mythunga is a close relative of the Australian pterosaur Ferrodraco.
facts.quote: It is a close relative of Ferrodraco, another Australian anhanguerid.

facts.statement: At the time of its redescription, Mythunga was the most completely known pterosaur from Australia, a continent with fewer than twenty known pterosaur fossils.
facts.quote: At that time it was still the most completely known pterosaur of Australia. No more than twenty pterosaur fossils were known from that continent, most of them teeth and bone fragments.

facts.statement: In 2010, Alexander Kellner and colleagues placed Mythunga within the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: En 2010, Alexander Kellner y sus colegas ubicaron a Mythunga dentro de Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: A 2019 phylogenetic analysis by Pentland et al. recovered Mythunga as a member of the family Ornithocheiridae, specifically within the subfamily Ornithocheirinae as the sister taxon to Ferrodraco.
facts.quote: Los resultados de un análisis filogenético realizado por Pentland et al. (2019) han recuperado a Mythunga como miembro de la familia Ornithocheiridae, más precisamente dentro de la subfamilia Ornithocheirinae como taxón hermano de Ferrodraco.

facts.statement: However, a 2020 study by Borja Holgado and Rodrigo Pêgas reclassified Mythunga within the family Anhangueridae, specifically in the subfamily Tropeognathinae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio realizado por Borja Holgado y Rodrigo Pêgas en 2020 había vuelto a clasificar a Mythunga dentro de la familia Anhangueridae, más precisamente dentro de la subfamilia Tropeognathinae.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Mythunga as Tropeognathinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tropeognathinae

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the family of Mythunga as Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Family: Anhangueridae

facts.statement: Mythunga is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Mythunga is Mythunga camara.
facts.quote: Type species: Mythunga camara

facts.statement: Mythunga lived during the Albian stage, from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Mythunga was named by Molnar and Thulborn in 2007.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Mythunga (genus), Molnar and Thulborn 2007

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Mythunga is currently recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
